newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition faces another pre-poll blow.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition faces another pre-poll blow.

text.p: The opposition Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) suffered another blow on Thursday ahead of general elections when it was ordered to pay Singapore $120,000 ($85,837) in damages for libelling its former leader.

But the ruling against the 12 members of SDP's central executive committee, including secretary general Chee Soon Juan and chairman Ling How Doong, will not bar them from the January 2 elections, as it was a civil and not a criminal case.
Ling and Chee refused to comment on the ruling, saying that they had an election campaign to run. "There is an appeal pending," Ling said.
Chee and three SDP leaders suffered their first blow on December 11 when parliament decided to fine them a total of Singapore $51,000 ($36,455) for contempt of parliament.

All four have paid the fines over a contention that government spending on health care had fallen to five percent of total expenditure on health. The correct figure was 25 percent and Chee put the error down to a typing mistake.

In his hour-long judgment, Justice T.S. Sinnathuray said: "The sum of $120,000 will assuage the injured feelings and restore the reputation" of Chiam See Tong, former secretary general and founder of SDP.

The judge said Chiam could claim "compensatory" and not "aggravated" damages which he asked for. During the 16-day trial, Chiam initially sought Singapore $250,000 in damages, which his lawyer raised to S$350,000.
Chiam's suit arose from a press statement the SDP issued on November 6, 1995 following his response to the party's challenge that he should resign.
Chiam said he would resign if Chee faced him in a by-election in a constituency where Chiam is the member of parliament in a winner-take-all contest for party leadership.
The statement said Chee would accept the challenge if Chiam joined the ruling People's Action party (PAP) and stood as its candidate.
It added that "of late Chiam has been highly praised by the PAP and he has also been very supportive of the ruling party in attacking the SDP".

Chiam said the statement implied that he was a PAP puppet, stooge or lackey, that he had compromised his principles and integrity as an opposition MP and was motivated by a quest for personal political power.
Justice Sinnathuray said he found the statement aimed to embarrass Chiam and showed malice by some SDP leaders.

Chiam later told reporters: "We think that the judgement is very good, very sound and very balanced. The whole idea of a defamatory action is to clear one's name and I think that I've cleared my name, honour and integrity."

Asked if the timing of the verdict before elections would give the impression the opposition was in disarray, Chiam said: "This defamatory action is personal to me and has nothing to do with election issues...this whole matter will have to be put to rest for the time being until elections are over."
